name: Quang Ngai food guide
summary: Don is the bowl where the Trà Khúc meets the sea. Báo Văn hóa peaks it in May and June. Vietnam Airlines prints 15,000–30,000 VND for a cooked bowl and builds it differently. Kẹo gương, mạch nha, đường phèn, and đường phổi are the sweets to carry home. An hour or a price that was not printed is Check on arrival.
body: Báo Văn hóa scrubs the shells, soaks out the sand, and boils don until it opens, then puts the meat back with sliced onion and rice paper. Fish sauce and xiêm chili are enough, it says, because mật don is the sweetness. Yellow shells and black shells are both named. Vietnam Airlines cooks the same animal with hành tăm and serves grilled rice paper, herbs, and fried shallot. ZaloPay pours the broth over chopped hành tăm and says morning or evening. The end of Trường Sa is the Báo Văn hóa spot. The culture office’s festival ground is a different bank, south of cầu Cổ Lũy.

The Cẩm Thành ward article’s proverb is kẹo gương Thu Xà, mạch nha Thi Phổ (Mộ Đức). Cá bống sông Trà is kho tiêu on Vietnam Airlines, a dry rim in a box on the same article, and rim mặn ngọt on the ward article. Those are not one recipe. The rural-tourism article on vietnamtourism.gov.vn sets đường phèn for seven days and calls đường phổi the airy piece.

Lý Sơn, Sa Huỳnh, Trà Bồng, and Ba Tơ are not the river breakfast. Vietnam Airlines prices cúm núm, gỏi tỏi, cá tà ma, mắm nhum, cua Huỳnh Đế, tỏi, and quế on those coasts and streams. Sở Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch also names hến, ram chả cá, bắp xào, trứng vịt lộn, bánh căn, bánh cuốn, cá viên chiên, chè, and đậu hũ at the don festival and does not describe them. A method for those is Check on arrival.
specialtiesLead: Don and the Trà Khúc fish come first, then the small bánh xèo, the corn roll, and the sugar sweets. Lý Sơn, Sa Huỳnh, and the mountain streams follow.

sections.heading: City specialties
paragraphs: These are the plates with a published method. The culture office, on a notice dated 23 July 2026, also names hến, ram chả cá, bắp xào, trứng vịt lộn, bánh căn, bánh cuốn, cá viên chiên, chè, and đậu hũ at Lễ hội Don An Phú and does not describe them. A method for those is Check on arrival. The Nghĩa Hành article names bánh phồng and cơm rang from cá bống sông Trà and does not describe them either.

spots.name: Don
spots.note: Don is the brackish bivalve where the Trà Khúc meets the sea. Báo Văn hóa calls that water nước chè hai, peaks the season in May and June, and builds the bowl with onion and rice paper. Vietnam Airlines cooks it with hành tăm and prints a price. ZaloPay pours the broth over chopped hành tăm. Vietnam Airlines prints 75,000 VND for 250 g prepared, with nước cốt, and 15,000–30,000 VND for a cooked bowl. Báo Văn hóa and ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca bong kho tieu
spots.nameVi: Cá bống sông Trà kho tiêu
spots.note: Cá bống sông Trà kho tiêu is the pepper braise. Vietnam Airlines uses green pepper, fish sauce, and caramel. ZaloPay adds fresh chili. The Cẩm Thành ward article’s phrase is a salty-sweet braise, printed separately. Vietnam Airlines prints 160,000 VND for 300 g of the pepper braise. ZaloPay and the ward article printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca bong rim
spots.note: Vietnam Airlines describes cá bống sông Trà rimmed until dry, as a gift box. The Cẩm Thành ward article says cá bống sông Trà rim mặn ngọt and does not give the dry-box method. The two lines are both printed. Vietnam Airlines prints 90,000 VND for a 200 g box. The ward article printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh xeo
spots.note: Quảng Ngãi bánh xèo is the small cake, not the large southern crepe. Vietnam Airlines pours a thin rice batter into a hot iron pan. ZaloPay says a clay mold. The culture office names the cake and does not describe it. Vietnam Airlines prints from 12,000 VND a cake. ZaloPay and the culture office printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ram bap
spots.note: Ram bắp is the young-corn roll. Vietnam Airlines fills it with pork, shrimp, and corn. ZaloPay names young corn, scallion, a little flour, and thin rice paper, and does not name pork or shrimp. Vietnam Airlines prints 80,000 VND for 500 g. ZaloPay and the culture office printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Com ga
spots.note: Cơm gà, as Vietnam Airlines describes it, is turmeric-tinted rice cooked in the water used to boil the chicken, with chicken boiled just done. Some kitchens also serve roti chicken or chicken offal. Vietnam Airlines prints 30,000–70,000 VND a portion. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bun ca ngu
spots.note: Vietnam Airlines describes bún cá ngừ um, tuna braised with turmeric and chili and poured over noodles. ZaloPay describes bún cá ngừ as a clear bone broth with tomato and pineapple. The two bowls are both printed. Vietnam Airlines prints from 25,000 VND a bowl. ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ram thit nuong
spots.note: Ram thịt nướng, as Vietnam Airlines describes it, is marinated pork rolled in thin rice paper and grilled over charcoal. It names the plate for holidays and for guests. Vietnam Airlines prints from 100,000 VND for a portion for three people. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh beo
spots.note: The culture office names bánh bèo at the Don An Phú festival and does not describe it. ZaloPay says the Quảng Ngãi cake has a thicker batter than the Hue cake, a shrimp-and-pork topping, and a small aluminum spoon. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Oc hut
spots.note: The culture office names ốc hút at the Don An Phú festival and does not say which snail or how it is cooked. ZaloPay describes a spicy plate of small apple snails with lemongrass, chili, garlic, and coconut water. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Sweets to carry home
paragraphs: Thu Xà is the candy in the proverb. Mộ Đức is the malt. The rock sugar and the airy sugar sit in villages along the Trà Khúc. Vietnam Airlines also names bánh thuẫn and bánh in beside bánh nổ and does not describe them. A method for those two is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Keo guong
spots.note: Kẹo gương is the sugar candy from Thu Xà in the proverb on the Cẩm Thành ward article. Vietnam Airlines builds it from cane sugar, peanuts, and ginger. A ZaloPay caption instead names malt and sesame. Vietnam Airlines prints 35,000 VND for a 150 g box. The ward article and ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mach nha
spots.note: Mạch nha is the malt from Mộ Đức. The Cẩm Thành ward article pairs it with Thi Phổ in the proverb and says it is eaten with rice paper. A second ward article prints the sprout-and-reduce method. No price was printed. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Duong phen
spots.note: Đường phèn is the rock sugar. The rural-tourism article on vietnamtourism.gov.vn describes white and yellow crystals and a seven-day set. The Cẩm Thành ward article calls it a court tribute. Vietnam Airlines names đường phèn Phổ Hòa and prints no price. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Duong phoi
spots.note: Đường phổi is the airy cane sugar, named for a lung-like shape. The rural-tourism article on vietnamtourism.gov.vn says it is crisp, unlike clear hard rock sugar, and is used in chè, ginger water, or as a gift. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh bo
spots.note: Bánh bó, as Vietnam Airlines describes it, is roasted glutinous rice milled fine and packed with candied ginger, candied winter melon, peanuts, and sesame. Vietnam Airlines prints 30,000 VND for a 300 g bag. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh no
spots.note: Bánh nổ, as Vietnam Airlines describes it, is popped roasted glutinous rice pressed with cane sugar and ginger. It calls the cake a spring snack. The same article also lists bánh nổ again among gifts, with bánh thuẫn and bánh in, and does not describe those two. Vietnam Airlines prints 30,000 VND for a 250 g bag. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Xu xoa
spots.note: Xu xoa is the cool seaweed sweet. Vietnam Airlines uses sea grapes from around Lý Sơn, palm sugar, ginger, and coconut milk. ZaloPay describes a pale-brown jelly with reduced syrup and coconut milk, and does not name palm sugar or ginger. Vietnam Airlines prints 30,000 VND for a 500 g box. ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Banh it la gai
spots.note: Bánh ít lá gai, as ZaloPay describes it, is a small cake in banana leaf: a black dough of pounded ramie leaf and sticky rice, with mung bean or coconut. It names the cake for Tết, weddings, and offerings. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Regional dishes
paragraphs: These are specialties of Lý Sơn, Sa Huỳnh, Trà Bồng, and Ba Tơ. They are not stalls on Tôn Đức Thắng. Vietnam Airlines prints the seafood prices. The provincial introduction names cá niêng, ốc đá, rượu đót, hải sâm, cau from Sơn Hà and Sơn Tây, chè Minh Long, and dứa Ba Tơ, and does not describe a plate. A method for those is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cum num
spots.note: Cúm núm, as Vietnam Airlines describes it, is a round-shelled crab at Sa Huỳnh, firm and rich. The busy season it prints is lunar months 6 through 8. Vietnam Airlines prints 80,000 VND a kilogram. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Goi toi
spots.note: Gỏi tỏi is the young-garlic salad on Lý Sơn. Vietnam Airlines steams the garlic, shreds it, and mixes in boiled shrimp, pork belly, and rau răm. ZaloPay treats shrimp and pork as optional and does not say the garlic is steamed. Vietnam Airlines prints 120,000 VND a plate. ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Toi Ly Son
spots.note: Tỏi Lý Sơn is the island garlic Vietnam Airlines describes: small bulbs, even cloves, smooth white skin, a strong smell, and a mild heat. It also names single-clove garlic, black garlic, garlic wine, and garlic in honey. Vietnam Airlines prints 150,000–190,000 VND a kilogram. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca ta ma
spots.note: Cá tà ma, as Vietnam Airlines describes it, is a small soft fish from deep water at Lý Sơn and Bình Châu. The grilled plate comes with rice paper, herbs, and green chili salt. Vietnam Airlines prints from 250,000 VND a kilogram. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Mam nhum
spots.note: Mắm nhum is fermented sea-urchin. Vietnam Airlines says about one month in a clay jar. ZaloPay says many months, names Sa Huỳnh, and starts from the gut rather than the red meat. Vietnam Airlines prints 200,000 for a 200 g jar and does not print a currency word on that line. ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Cua Huynh De
spots.note: Cua Huỳnh Đế is the deep-water crab. Vietnam Airlines describes a red-pink thick shell, white meat, and rich roe, and prints a wide price. ZaloPay places it at Sa Huỳnh and Lý Sơn and adds a hotpot. Vietnam Airlines prints 900,000–1,800,000 VND a kilogram, depending on type and size. ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ca nien
spots.address: Sơn Hà, Trà Bồng, Tây Trà, and Ba Tơ
spots.note: Cá niên is the mountain-stream fish. Vietnam Airlines places it in Sơn Hà, Trà Bồng, and Tây Trà, and spells the rainy season as lunar April to August. ZaloPay places it in Trà Bồng and Ba Tơ. The provincial introduction spells cá niêng and does not describe a plate. Vietnam Airlines prints 300,000–800,000, and the currency word on that line is VDN, a kilogram, fresh or frozen. ZaloPay printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Que Tra Bong
spots.note: Quế Trà Bồng is the cinnamon Vietnam Airlines says holds a geographical indication, grown in Trà Bồng on more than 1,700 hectares. The provincial introduction calls the same bark fragrant and warm and prints no area and no price. Vietnam Airlines prints 55,000 VND a kilogram for dried bark, 150,000 VND for 500 g of powder, and 200,000 VND for 10 ml of oil. The provincial introduction printed no price. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Ruou can
spots.note: The provincial introduction names rượu cần in the mountains, beside rượu đót. ZaloPay describes the Hre jar in Ba Tơ: forest-leaf yeast, upland sticky rice, and a clay jar. No strength and no price were printed. The price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Casual dining
paragraphs: Phố đêm Sông Trà is the weekend street on Tôn Đức Thắng. Don at the end of Trường Sa is a different bank from the festival ground south of cầu Cổ Lũy. Chợ Quảng Ngãi is where Vietnam Airlines says to buy specialties.

spots.name: Song Tra night street
spots.note: About 300 m, 17:00–22:00 on Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and holidays. The provincial portal runs it from Công viên Thạch Bích to cầu Thạch Bích and dates the opening to the evening of 6 February 2026. Báo Lao Động puts the stalls on the east side of the bridge and counts 72 stalls, 40 of them food and non-alcohol drinks. VnExpress had said around 7 February. No entry fee was printed.

spots.name: Truong Sa river mouth
spots.note: Báo Văn hóa puts don here, where the river meets the sea. The peak it prints is May and June. A daily hour was not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

spots.name: Quang Ngai market
spots.note: Vietnam Airlines prints 159 Nguyễn Bá Loan, Nguyễn Ngiêm, as the market for specialties. Hours were not printed. The hour is Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Vietnam Airlines calls bún cá ngừ um breakfast or a light lunch. ZaloPay uses the same meals for a different bún cá ngừ. ZaloPay also says don is eaten in the morning or the evening, and says bánh xèo is eaten at breakfast as well as later. Báo Văn hóa prints no clock for don. The hour is Check on arrival.

seoTitle: Quang Ngai food guide — don and the sugar sweets
seoDescription: Don where the Trà Khúc meets the sea, cá bống, kẹo gương, and mạch nha. Vietnam Airlines prints some prices. An unprinted hour is Check on arrival.
